entities.summary: Andrea Mantegna was an Italian painter, archaeologist, and artist of the Early Renaissance. He was born in 1431 or 1435 in Isola di Río, near Mantua, in the Duchy of Milan. Mantegna's work was influenced by classical Roman and Greek art, and he was a key figure in the development of Renaissance humanism. He studied Roman law and archaeology, and his work often featured ancient Roman and Greek subjects, as well as biblical scenes. Mantegna's artistic style, which blended realism and idealism, was influential in the development of Western art. He was a prolific artist, producing over 300 paintings, including portraits, landscapes, and mythological scenes. Mantegna's most famous works include his altarpieces for the Franciscan church in Mantua and his frescoes in the Palazzo Ducale in Mantua. Mantegna's legacy extends beyond his artistic achievements, as he played a significant role in the cultural and intellectual renewal of Italy during the Renaissance. As a patron of the arts, Mantegna supported many artists, including his fellow painter, Jacopo Bellini, and his pupil, Lorenzo Lotto. Mantegna's art continues to inspire and influence artists to this day, and his contributions to the development of Western art remain unparalleled.
